extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic (mathematical logicians, researchers aiming to publish in BSL)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and preparation rules for manuscripts to The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic, covering authorship, file formats, prior-publication policies, accessibility, ethics, and publication/licensing options. Intended to guide authors preparing initial and final versions for submission and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identity and AI authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed author of a submission to the BSL must be an identifiable human being. Anonymous authorship is not permitted. Pseudonyms are permitted as long as the editors receive full and accurate information about the name and contact data for the author. No Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool can be listed as an author of any submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any use of AI tools in the research for, or the preparation of, the submission should be fully acknowledged and described to editors and readers where relevant and in the Acknowledgements section. Use of other general aids, human or machine, in translation, writing or editing should be acknowledged in Acknowledgements. This requirement does not apply to standard word processing or translation programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship approval and exclusivity of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are accepted for review with the understanding that all persons listed as authors have given their approval for the submission of the paper, and that the same work (1) has not been published elsewhere; (2) is not presently submitted or accepted for publication elsewhere; and (3) will not be submitted elsewhere unless the manuscript is either withdrawn from or rejected by the BSL first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed author takes responsibility for the content and its compliance with general submission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility for ethical and legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed author takes responsibility for the manuscript's content and its compliance with general guidelines for submissions to the BSL including expectations for proper citations, copyright rules and avoidance of conflicts or interest, defamation, bias, harassment or plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of and abide by the Association’s general publication ethics policies (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID identifiers encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors strongly encourage that submitted manuscripts include ORCID identifiers for all authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID identifiers help data collection systems identify and credit authors and are used by funders to identify proper acknowledgements. If you don’t have an ORCID identifier, see ORCID for information and sign-up links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on extending prior conference publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Full versions of important papers that have previously been published in conference proceedings are eligible for publication, provided that the submitted paper extends the prior publication in a significant way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors submit such a paper they are required to provide a precise reference to the prior publication and to explain how the submission differs from the conference version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for submitting shorter conference versions after journal submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who have submitted a paper and then want to submit a shorter version to a conference should notify the editor and supply a copy of the version to be submitted to the conference and explain how the submission differs from the conference version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The previously submitted paper must still meet the requirement of extending the new conference version in a significant way. If the conference version is accepted before the journal version, the journal editor should be notified with details. If the journal submission is accepted before publication of the conference version, the conference version should include a statement that the full version has been accepted by the journal; if already published in the journal, full bibliographic information should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of prior editor rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper has been previously rejected by one of the editors, this fact must be disclosed to any new editor to whom it, or a revised version, is being submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Association publication ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be aware of, and abide by, the Association’s general publication ethics policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to the Association’s policies is provided; compliance is expected as part of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system and language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles and communications should be submitted via the BSL EditFlow Management System. Authors should follow the specific procedures indicated there. As of January 1, 2023 only papers in English will be considered for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you experience technical difficulties with the journal management system, contact EditFlow technical help; larger issues can be sent to the publisher email provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and figure restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be PDF documents. Color is not allowed. Hand-drawn figures or diagrams are generally not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be made for professionally drawn diagrams—consult with your editor if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred typesetting and style files
rubrics_metrics.description: It is by far best to prepare manuscripts in some version of TeX. The relevant ASL style files can be found at the Author Resources page and can be used for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acceptance conversion to this style for the final submitted version will provide a better idea of the typeset appearance of the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate formats and source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Formats other than TeX may be acceptable if all mathematical symbols, formulas etc. are entered in equation insertion mode for variants of Word or using MathType for word processors that support it. The source file (e.g. .doc or .docx) will also be required at submission. For submissions prepared in TeX, the .tex file is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final-version metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts are required for final versions of all papers. AMS classification numbers (MSC 2020) and keywords are also required. If appropriate, ACM CCS designators are strongly recommended. So too are ORCID identifiers for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing the final version include full postal addresses for each author with an institutional affiliation where the research was performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alt-text and accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with new regulations in the EU and USA final versions of accepted papers are required to have explanations/descriptions of all diagrams, tables and other displayed material called alt-text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines from Cambridge University Press (CUP) and examples are linked. The alt-text will not appear in typical on-screen or printed versions but will be available to screen readers and other accessibility aids. Authors can add alt-text themselves or have CUP’s system provide acceptable alt-text which authors can check for correctness during galley proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical help and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: If you experience technical difficulties with the journal management system, please contact the technical help resources at EditFlow. More global or abstract problems can be sent to the publisher (email provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright, licensing, and open access options
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors retain copyright in published articles but before publication they will be required to sign a license to publish agreement with the Association for Symbolic Logic. The Journal is now a hybrid publication and so there will be a choice of the type of license. All publications are eligible for the science journal version of CUP’s Green Open Access. Gold Open access is available for a fee (APC) or under certain read-and-publish agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If eligible for gold open access and your funder/institution does not require an unrestricted CC-By license, the editors suggest choosing a license that does not automatically allow commercial use or distribution (e.g., CC-By-NC-ND) to better control unwanted commercial uses. Further details will be supplied upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance author materials and access
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication, authors will receive a link to a freely accessible electronic PDF file of the published paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details about publication and licensing arrangements will be supplied upon acceptance.
